clinician.trajectory_summary: A 59-year-old man presented with a 5-month history of progressive neurological symptoms including behavior disturbances, insomnia, memory impairment, disorientation, visual hallucinations, myoclonus, and frequent faciobrachial dystonic seizures (FBDS). Initial workup revealed a normal brain MRI (E002) and initially normal CSF findings (E004). EEG showed disorganization and slowing of background activity (E003). Given the clinical picture, autoantibody testing was performed, which revealed high titers of serum anti-voltage-gated potassium channel (VGKC)-complex antibodies (678.3 pmol/L), with LGI1 antibodies identified as the specific antigenic target, confirming the diagnosis of VGKC-complex antibody limbic encephalitis (E008). Anti-CASPR2 antibodies were negative (E008). Initial treatments for hyponatremia and various antiepileptic drugs (phenytoin, piracetam, levetiracetam, carbamazepine) were either ineffective, caused side effects, or were contraindicated (E011). The patient was then started on immunotherapy with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) (0.4 g/kg daily for 5 days). After 1 month, he responded significantly, becoming seizure-free and showing marked cognitive improvement, with his MMSE score increasing to 27/30. He remained relapse-free during 18 months of follow-up, and antiepileptic treatment was progressively diminished (E012).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with a constellation of neurological symptoms including behavior disturbances, insomnia, memory impairment, disorientation, visual hallucinations, myoclonus, and faciobrachial dystonic seizures (FBDS).
Brain MRI was unremarkable for hippocampal lesions.
Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis was initially normal.
Electroencephalography (EEG) showed disorganization and slowing of background activity without periodic synchronous discharges.
High titers of serum anti-voltage-gated potassium channel (VGKC)-complex antibodies were found (678.3 pmol/L).
LGI1 antibodies were identified as the specific antigenic target within the VGKC-complex.
Immunotherapy with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) led to significant clinical improvement, including becoming seizure-free and cognitive recovery.
Patient remained relapse-free for 18 months with progressive reduction of antiepileptic treatment.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Significant inflammatory or infectious CNS process (based on initial CSF)
